title: AlphaFold3-aided cryo-EM resolves native Anopheles salivary protein complexes
summary: Biochemical and mass-spectrometry analyses identified native interactions among Anopheles mosquito salivary proteins, including Saglin and SGS4/SGS5. AlphaFold predictions helped identify subunits, and AlphaFold3 models supplied initial structures for fitting into cryo-electron-microscopy density, followed by manual model building and refinement. The resulting Saglin–SGS4 structure and related complexes reveal native protein organization and partner-dependent conformations. AI assisted structural assignment; experimental maps and biochemical observations provide the direct evidence. The proposed relevance to malaria transmission remains a hypothesis: the study does not demonstrate parasite-invasion, transmission-blocking or clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: AlphaFold and AlphaFold 3 protein-structure prediction, used to guide subunit identification and cryo-EM model building
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

evidence.tested: Mass spectrometry and biochemical analyses of native mosquito salivary-gland extracts/saliva established SGS4/SGS5 association with Saglin and other SG1 proteins; cryo-EM structures were fit and manually adjusted against experimental density. AlphaFold3 predictions supplied initial structural models and supported protein identification/model construction.
evidence.unknown: No in vivo parasite-invasion, infection, or transmission-blocking assay is reported in this paper; the proposed role of the complexes in transmission is not established by these structural studies. AI-predicted structures were fitted into cryo-EM maps and are not alone the experimental finding.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold predictions, including AlphaFold3 models, were used to help identify Saglin and build protein models into cryo-EM density, contributing to structural assignment of the newly characterized native protein complexes.

source_review.scope: Primary open-access article abstract, relevant native-complex Results, AlphaFold3/cryo-EM model-building Methods, affiliation/date metadata and functional-limitation context independently read; no pathogen experiments or independent reanalysis.
